title: ChangeResult + withFileLock + atomicWriteJson trích ra
wave: M4 Wave B — Ghi trạng thái bền vững và sự thật của bảng settings (shippable: false)
one_line: Plugin enable/disable/setting writes become a locked read-modify-write that reports back whether the change actually landed on disk, and the ad-hoc atomic-JSON writer becomes one shared utility.
user_visible_effect: Toggling a plugin in /settings now returns a real answer instead of an unconditional void: the caller learns whether the lockfile actually changed and whether the running session picked it up. A second writer can no longer silently clobber a first writer's plugin toggle. Note that M4 Wave B is `shippable: false` (plan section 6.2) — this is an observable behaviour change and may not ship until M4's single changelog decision is authorized.

steps.instruction: Build the native addon FIRST — `bun --cwd=packages/natives run build`. Without it every test in this item is unrunnable, because `packages/utils/src/file-lock.ts:9` imports `FileLock` from `@oh-my-pi/pi-natives` and any test that touches `withFileLock` dies with 'Failed to load pi_natives native addon for darwin-arm64'. Confirm with `bun test packages/utils/test/file-lock.test.ts` going from 0 pass / 1 fail to green before writing any code.

Create `packages/utils/src/atomic-write.ts` and move the `atomicWriteJson` body into it verbatim (the 2-space JSON stringify plus trailing newline, the `${filePath}.tmp` temp path, the `fs.rename`, the EPERM unlink-then-rename fallback, and the tmp cleanup on unexpected errors). Keep the existing `(err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "EPERM"` cast — it is not `any` and AGENTS.md permits it. Add `export * from "./atomic-write";` to the utils barrel in alphabetical position. Then delete the original from registry.ts:44-71 and point its two callers at the shared import.

Add the exported `ChangeResult` interface (`{ changed: boolean; application: "applied" | "restart-required" }`) to manager.ts. Add the private `#mutateConfig(mutate, application)` helper (see code_shape) that opens `withFileLock(getPluginsLockfile(), ...)`, re-reads the config from disk INSIDE the lock via the existing `#loadRuntimeConfig()`, snapshots it, applies the caller's mutation to the fresh object, diffs to compute `changed`, adopts the fresh object as `this.#runtimeConfig`, and writes with `atomicWriteJson` only when `changed`. Delete `#saveRuntimeConfig`. Import `withFileLock` and `atomicWriteJson` from `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils` at the top level — no inline imports.

Convert the four public mutators to the new shape. This is the mechanical part and the part the plan gets wrong: each one currently mutates the memoized `this.#runtimeConfig` and THEN calls save. You must move the mutation INSIDE the callback — leave a `config.plugins[name].enabled = enabled` sitting outside the lock and the helper will read fresh state, apply nothing, diff nothing, and report `changed: false` while silently dropping the write. `deletePluginSetting` (:954) currently guards its save behind `if (config.settings[name])`; drop the guard and let the diff produce `changed: false` for the missing-key case.

Convert the remaining five writers — install (:668), uninstall (:724), link (:855), `#removeInvalidFeature` (:1221), `#removeOrphanedConfig` (:1231) — to pass their mutation into `#mutateConfig`. The two private helpers already return booleans; keep that shape and return the `ChangeResult` alongside rather than replacing it. After this step `git grep -n saveRuntimeConfig -- packages/` must return zero hits — that is the mechanical proof the refactor is complete.

Widen the three `PluginSettingsManager` mutator return types to `Promise<ChangeResult>` and import the type. Where should the type come from is open question 1 — if tui cannot import from coding-agent (it cannot; the dependency runs the other way), declare it in tui and have coding-agent's manager satisfy it structurally, exactly as the interface is satisfied today. Then consume the result at the overlay call sites (:776, :786, :790, :823).

Make the four CLI mutating commands act on the result instead of discarding it — at minimum report `application: "restart-required"` so a user who toggles a plugin from the shell learns the running session did not change. This is user-visible and belongs in the changelog entry.

Write the tests per test_contract. Non-negotiable: the negative control. Without it the two-instance test proves nothing, because two commands on ONE instance already both land (the memoized object is shared) — the plan is right about this and it is the single easiest way to ship a green test suite that guards nothing.

Reconcile with M3-A4. Either M3-A4 has not landed — in which case this PR and M3-A4 must be one PR or have an explicit merge order, because both rewrite setPluginSetting — or it has landed and this step is a rebase. Whichever way, `grep -c secret packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/plugins/manager.ts` must be 0 before and after; that is M3's regression guard and it is already 0 at baseline, so it guards a future regression rather than proving anything today.

Run the full gate. Do not mark done until every command below passes. `bun run check:ts` currently passes clean on this tree — if it goes red, the tui/coding-agent interface drift is real and must be fixed here, not deferred.

test_contract:
Defends three named contracts.

(1) LOST-UPDATE ELIMINATION. Observable contract: after two independent PluginManager instances (each holding its OWN memoized config, both pointed at the same lockfile) run setEnabled concurrently, the JSON on disk contains BOTH changes. If it regresses, the user sees a plugin toggle silently vanish because another writer touched the lockfile first — the exact failure that motivated M4-4.

    Test geometry is load-bearing and the plan is right about it. `#ensureConfigLoaded` (manager.ts:141-146) memoizes `this.#runtimeConfig` per instance, so two setEnabled calls on ONE instance mutate one shared object and the second write necessarily contains both changes EVEN WITH THE LOCK ENTIRELY REMOVED. A single-instance test is therefore green on the unfixed code and defends nothing. The test must construct two PluginManager instances and assert each loads its own config. Note that `getPluginsLockfile` is a GLOBAL path (~/.omp/plugins/omp-plugins.lock.json via dirs.ts:652), NOT cwd-derived, so both instances must be pointed at one temp lockfile via the spyOn pattern.

(2) THE NEGATIVE CONTROL — mandatory, without it (1) proves nothing. Re-run scenario (1) against the PRE-fix algorithm, written out inline in the test as a plain mutate-then-Bun.write helper with no lock, and assert the disk file contains only ONE of the two changes. This is the row that makes (1) meaningful: it demonstrates the failure the lock removes, using the real file, the real path, and the real algorithm.

    Implementation constraint: drive this with an inline re-implementation, NOT by patching PluginManager. AGENTS.md bans `mock.module()` outright, and patching the class to remove its own lock would be the same kind of lie. The inline helper writes the same bytes to the same spied lockfile — that is a real reproduction, not a mock.

(3) ChangeResult SEMANTICS, one test per branch:
    - setEnabled to the value it already holds returns changed:false and leaves the file bytes untouched. (Distinct outcome from the success path — this is the branch that proves `changed` is observed on disk rather than echoing a returned flag.)
    - deletePluginSetting on an absent key returns changed:false.
    - setEnabled on an unknown plugin still rejects with /not found in runtime config/ AND leaves the file untouched — proving the throw happens inside the lock before any write, so a failed call cannot corrupt the lockfile.
    - setEnabled returns application: 'restart-required' (the no-HMR path).

Also assert, for the extracted helper: atomicWriteJson leaves no `.tmp` sibling behind and produces parseable JSON with the trailing newline. The Windows EPERM fallback is NOT testable on darwin-arm64 — do not fake it with a source grep or a forced errno; state it as untested here.

Full-suite safety: use the exact isolation pattern from packages/coding-agent/test/plugin-config.test.ts:19-33 — `spyOn(piUtils, 'getPluginsDir'|'getPluginsLockfile'|'getProjectDir'|'getProjectPluginOverridesPath')` in beforeEach, `mock.restore()` in afterEach, `fs.mkdtemp` under `os.tmpdir()` and `removeWithRetries` for cleanup. No file-wide mutation of `Bun.*` or `process.env`.

AGENTS.md compliance: every test here names a consumer-observable failure mode. Do not add a test that only asserts the constructor or the file exists. Do NOT source-grep manager.ts or registry.ts to prove the refactor happened — the `git grep saveRuntimeConfig` check in step 5 is a human checklist item, not a test.

Concretely, a reviewer must be able to show: (a) `bun test packages/utils/test/file-lock.test.ts` is green — it is 0 pass / 1 fail right now, so this alone is a real, currently-red gate; (b) the new test file passes AND its negative-control test asserts that the unlocked algorithm really does lose an update (temporarily delete `withFileLock` from `#mutateConfig` and confirm the contention test goes red — a gate that has never been seen red is not a gate); (c) `git grep -n saveRuntimeConfig -- packages/` returns zero hits; (d) `git grep -n atomicWriteJson -- packages/` shows exactly one definition, in packages/utils; (e) `grep -c secret .../manager.ts` is 0; (f) `bun run check:ts` is green, which is what actually catches the tui/coding-agent interface drift the plan warns about.

gate_can_fail: Yes, and three of the six steps are red today. Step 1-2 fail right now: the native addon is unbuilt, `withFileLock` imports `FileLock` from `@oh-my-pi/pi-natives` (file-lock.ts:9), and `bun test packages/utils/test/file-lock.test.ts` reports `0 pass, 1 fail` with 'Failed to load pi_natives native addon for darwin-arm64' — verified by running it. Step 5 is a genuine gate: it currently passes clean, and it is precisely what turns the tui interface drift into a build failure rather than a runtime surprise. The one step that is NOT self-validating is 6 — grep counts are a human checklist, not a test; if someone reorders the refactor so `#saveRuntimeConfig` is renamed rather than removed, the greps stay green while the lock is silently absent. The contention test with its negative control is the only real defense, and step 2 of the gate (delete the lock, watch it go red) is what proves that defense is live.

effort: M by the plan's own estimate. Realistically M-L: the mechanical part is large (nine call sites change shape, not just two signatures), and the test cannot be written or run until the native addon is built, which is a real chunk of wall-clock on a cold machine.
risk: The single most likely way to get this wrong is implementing the plan's words literally: 'wrap #saveRuntimeConfig in withFileLock and re-read the config inside the lock.' All nine call sites mutate the memoized `this.#runtimeConfig` BEFORE calling save — verified, e.g. setEnabled at 874-881 does `config.plugins[name].enabled = enabled;` then `await this.#saveRuntimeConfig();`. If you put a re-read inside the lock and write what comes back, the re-read CLOBBERS the caller's just-applied mutation. The result is a lock that serializes perfectly, a test that could still go green if you also kept the old object, and 100% of writes silently dropped in production. The mutation must move inside the locked section as a callback; there is no way to add the lock around the existing save and keep the existing call sites. Second-order risk: making `changed` an in-memory flag (`return changed` from the setter) rather than a disk-observed diff would make every test pass and the field meaningless — AGENTS.md calls this out explicitly and the plan calls it out too.
open_questions: Who decides `application: 'applied' | 'restart-required'`? `PluginManager` has no HMR knowledge and the string has zero referents in this repo (git grep 'restart-required' → 0 hits). The overlay path does only a PARTIAL reload: settings-selector.ts:1329 → selector-controller.ts:305-312 calls clearPluginRootsAndCaches + refreshSkillState + refreshSlashCommandState + resetCapabilities, but does NOT call `refreshAgentDiscovery`, which the real `reloadPlugins` does (acp-agent.ts:2167). So a toggle arguably half-applies. A human must decide: (a) PluginManager always returns 'restart-required' and the overlay upgrades to 'applied' when it knows a reload ran, (b) the value is computed at the tui layer, or (c) 'applied' is claimed once refreshAgentDiscovery is added to the settings path. The plan's model for this type is `packages/boot/plugin-manager/src/types.ts:111-114` — which DOES NOT EXIST in this repo (see plan_corrections).

Is `PluginSettingsMarketplaceManager.setPluginEnabled` in scope for the return-type change? The plan lists it as 'the fourth mutator', but it is implemented by a DIFFERENT class — `MarketplaceManager` at marketplace/manager.ts:686 — and writes the marketplace registry, not the plugins lockfile. It never touches `#saveRuntimeConfig`. It shares only the tui overlay package. Widening its return type is a separate breaking change with its own changelog weight.

Is `MarketplaceManager.#writeRuntimeConfig` (marketplace/manager.ts:923-925) in scope? It is a second runtime-config writer with the identical read-modify-write shape, no lock, and it does not go through `atomicWriteJson`. The plan never mentions it, but leaving it untouched is precisely the 'two implementations' violation the plan's own risk 2 warns about.

Should the extracted `atomicWriteJson` keep the FIXED `${filePath}.tmp` suffix, or move to the hardened `${filePath}.${process.pid}.${random}.tmp` form that packages/ai/src/auth-broker/snapshot-cache.ts:93 uses? A shared temp name is safe only while every writer of a given file takes the same lock — which is true for the lockfile after this change but NOT for the two marketplace registries, which do not lock. Worth deciding before the util becomes central.

Changelog sequencing: the plan (section 6.2) says M4 ships as ONE changelog decision covering Waves B, C and D, and that this plan never writes its own entries. So the three CHANGELOG.md edits above are placeholders to track, not work to do now. Confirm that reading before anyone adds an entry.

Does the `secret` guard belong in this PR's gate at all? `grep -c secret manager.ts` is already 0 at baseline, so it cannot distinguish 'M3-A4 landed' from 'M3-A4 never existed'. If M3-A4 lands after this PR, the guard is still worth keeping — but it should be described as a M3 guard this PR must not break, not as evidence about M3-A4's state.
